output.summary: A succulent coastal perennial of unspecified native origin, sea sandwort ranges around temperate and Arctic coasts of northern Europe, northern Asia and North America. It forms patches above the high-water mark, with branching stems buried in sand and paired fleshy leaves. Shoots and leaves are eaten raw, cooked or fermented; seeds are ground and added to flour or used as garnish.
